name: Independent re-verification of every sub-agent HANDOFF
mechanism: After every build sub-agent finished, re-run the actual verification commands (typecheck/test/lint) and read the actual diff, rather than trusting the sub-agent's self-reported pass/fail counts. A phase-validator sub-agent then independently re-checks exit conditions against the code, not the HANDOFF prose.
evidence: multi-worker-tasks campaign, all 6 phases (2026-09-04) — this discipline is what caught the first variant of the whole-instance-reopen bug (found during a disambiguation fix's own testing, then confirmed by Archon re-reading the diff) before the phase was marked complete
applicability: Any multi-phase Archon campaign delegating build work to sub-agents, especially ones touching shared/concurrent state logic

name: Convert manual smoke-test end conditions into permanent end-to-end regression tests
mechanism: Rather than performing a one-off manual click-through for an architecture doc's 'manual smoke test' end condition, write one integration test that drives the complete multi-step narrative through real HTTP routes against a live test database, asserting the full history/ledger trace. This preserves the verification as a permanent regression guard instead of a one-time click that leaves no trace.
evidence: multi-worker-tasks campaign Phase 5 (2026-09-04) — multi-worker-full-lifecycle.test.ts; this is exactly the kind of full-narrative test that caught a regression none of the earlier phases' isolated-mechanic tests staged
applicability: Any campaign phase whose end condition is phrased as a manual walkthrough of a multi-step business process

name: Mirror an existing correct implementation exactly when generalizing a parallel code path
mechanism: When fixing releaseOrRevokeAssignment's missing staffing-aware reopen logic, the fix copied executeBuyout.ts's staysStaffed gating pattern verbatim (same lock helper, same minRequired computation, same branch structure) rather than inventing a new approach. This kept EXACTLY(1) provably safe (min===max===1 can never reach the new branch) and made the fix trivially reviewable by diffing against a known-correct reference.
evidence: multi-worker-tasks campaign, reopen.ts fix (2026-09-04) — both bugs in this function were fixed by direct comparison against executeBuyout.ts's already-correct Phase 2 implementation
applicability: Generalizing a single-cardinality code path to N-cardinality when a sibling function already handles the N-cardinality case correctly

name: Additive DTO evolution instead of breaking renames
mechanism: When a DTO needed to expose a list instead of a single item (e.g. every active assignment instead of one), the existing singular field was kept unchanged (still the lowest-index entry, for backward compatibility) and a new plural field was added alongside it, rather than renaming/removing the singular field. This let backend phases ship independently of the frontend phase that would consume the new shape.
evidence: multi-worker-tasks campaign Phase 3 (2026-09-04) — activeAssignment/assignment/assignee kept, activeAssignments/assignees added
applicability: Any phased campaign where backend and frontend consumption of a widened DTO happen in separate phases

name: Unordered findFirst on a status filter that can match more than one row
what-was-tried: Three admin routes fetched 'the' ACTIVE/COMPLETED TaskAssignment for an instance via findFirst with no orderBy and no way to specify which one, correct only when the filter matches at most one row.
failure-mode: Once a feature made more than one row able to match the same filter (multiple concurrent ACTIVE assignments per instance), the query silently picked an arbitrary one instead of erroring or requiring disambiguation — this had no automated coverage because no prior test had ever staged more than one matching row.
avoidance: When adding a feature that lets a previously-1:1 relationship become 1:N, grep for every findFirst/find-the-single-X query against the changed relationship and either add an explicit disambiguating id or a hard multiplicity check that errors loudly rather than picking arbitrarily

name: Whole-entity state mutated from a single related-row event without an aggregate check
what-was-tried: releaseOrRevokeAssignment flipped the entire TaskInstance to AVAILABLE whenever any one TaskAssignment closed, without checking how many other assignments were still active on the same instance.
failure-mode: Once an instance could hold more than one concurrent active assignment, closing one incorrectly reset the whole instance's status even though co-assignees were still actively working it — violating the campaign's own stated staffing invariant. A second, narrower variant of the same missing-aggregate-check root cause (the function's top-level guard assumed the instance could only be ASSIGNED, never AVAILABLE-with-an-active-slot) was found later by live testing, not by any automated test.
evidence: multi-worker-tasks campaign Phase 4-5 (2026-09-04) — reopen.ts's releaseOrRevokeAssignment, two fix rounds
avoidance: When an entity's status is derived from the state of multiple child rows, any mutation triggered by a single child row changing must recompute the aggregate (count/sum/etc.) before deciding whether the parent's status should also change — never assume the mutating child is the only one

name: Denormalized field not copied at every entity-creation path
what-was-tried: Two new fields (workerCountMode, workerCount) were added to TaskInstance and correctly used by every use-case that reads them, but neither of the two real code paths that create a TaskInstance (auto-materialization sweep, manual admin materialize endpoint) was updated to copy the values from the parent TaskDefinition.
failure-mode: Every instance created through a real path silently reverted to the schema default, making the feature completely inert end-to-end for two full phases, undetected because the phase's own tests created instances directly via a DB insert that bypassed both real creation paths.
evidence: multi-worker-tasks campaign Phase 3 (2026-09-04) — runAssignmentSweep.ts T1 materialization and admin.ts's /materialize endpoint
avoidance: When adding a new field to an entity, grep for every .create() call site for that entity's table, not just the use-cases that read the new field, and verify each one either sets it explicitly or is provably fine relying on the schema default

name: Inconsistent delegation telemetry logging within a single orchestrator session
what-was-tried: Archon logged campaign-start and Phase 1-2's agent-start/agent-complete events to telemetry-log.cjs, but Phase 3 onward (including two corrective-fix delegations and five phase-validator spawns) used the Agent tool directly without the paired telemetry calls the protocol specifies.
failure-mode: The raw agent-runs.jsonl telemetry for this campaign now understates how much delegation and independent-verification work actually happened, and even contains a stray premature campaign-complete event logged mid-Phase-3 from an earlier session attempt — making the telemetry trail unreliable as a record of this campaign's actual activity.
avoidance: Call telemetry-log.cjs --event agent-start/agent-complete around every Agent tool delegation and validator spawn for the full duration of a campaign, not only its first phases

what: apps/api/src/domain/task/state-machine.ts marked a hard no-touch file for the entire campaign
rationale: Isolating the highest-regression-risk file (the exhaustively-tested core state machine) and proving zero-diff every phase was chosen as the primary regression-safety strategy, over trying to extend the state machine itself for multi-worker semantics.
outcome: completed — zero-diff maintained and independently re-verified across all 6 phases, no regression ever traced to this file

what: AT_MOST implies a floor of 1 (mirrors today's single-worker guarantee); AT_LEAST has no ceiling
rationale: Two open questions from the PRD were resolved concretely in the architecture doc rather than left for a mid-build question, reasoning that AT_MOST should never let a task go fully unstaffed the way EXACTLY already guarantees, while AT_LEAST's whole purpose is unbounded recruiting.
outcome: completed — implemented consistently in worker-slots.ts and never caused an incorrect behavior in testing, but the interpretation itself was never confirmed by the actual household/user and remains an open Review Queue item post-completion

what: Architecture doc's Phase 4 file list was extended beyond its literal contents (added apps/web/src/api/types.ts and the actual admin edit form file) rather than treated as fixed scope
rationale: The architecture doc named only the read-only TaskMaintenanceCard and missed the actual create/edit form component and the hand-maintained admin type declarations; the phase's end conditions were literally unreachable without touching them.
outcome: completed — logged explicitly as a documentation gap rather than scope creep, no rework needed

name: ambiguous-findfirst-on-multi-cardinality-status
message: findFirst filtered by a status that more than one row can hold (e.g. multiple ACTIVE TaskAssignments per instance) can silently pick an arbitrary row unless ordered or given an explicit id — see multi-worker-tasks campaign, 2026-09-04 (admin.ts revoke-assignment/complete/reject-completion). Add an explicit id parameter or an orderBy plus a multiplicity check.
